target_customer: Toronto car owners and fleets such as Uber and Car2Go drivers needing on demand repairs
problem: Car owners lacked trust and time for shop visits; Fiix sent a mechanic to the home or office.
business_model: Service marketplace charging for parts and labor, priced about 30 percent below dealerships

founders.name: Zain Manji
founders.background_notes: From YC page; announced the sale on Medium.

founders.name: Khallil Mangalji
founders.background_notes: Entered YC by pitching on Snapchat and built the startup while fighting cancer (BetaKit). BetaKit says the team included alumni of Apple, Google, Facebook, Instagram and Deloitte, not attributed per person.

exit.reason: Founders said expanding to new cities and improving retention needed large capital, and an American partner could extend the effort.

competitors.name: YourMechanic
competitors.what: On demand mobile mechanic, YC W12
competitors.traction_then: Launched 2012, operating in many US cities

technical_complexity.rationale: Booking, dispatch and quoting app; difficulty lay in mechanic quality and operations.

defensibility.rationale: Local mechanic supply and reviews helped slightly but US rivals were better funded and could enter Toronto.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A US competitor bought Fiix in autumn 2019 and Wrench later stopped serving Toronto.

market_need_then: Fiix reported over a million dollars in yearly sales and over a thousand customers in Toronto by March 2017 (TechCrunch), with about 8,000 customers by 2019.

branding.domain_note: Used fiix.io; a CBC article misspelled the name Fixx and a CMMS company Fiix also exists.

identity.voice_and_tone: Trust focused, framed as an Uber for mechanics

branding.community_and_virality: Founders drew attention by pitching YC through Justin Kan's Snapchat; over 500 five star reviews.

brand_strength.rationale: Local brand with good reviews but a name easily confused with a larger same name CMMS company and no wider coverage.

outcome_analysis: Fiix grew to about 8,000 customers in the Toronto area after a 1.8 million dollar seed in 2017 but remained confined to one metro. The founders said expanding and keeping consumers needed substantial capital and acquisition was costly, so they sold to Wrench in autumn 2019 for an undisclosed price. Wrench no longer serves Toronto, so the exit ended the service in that market.
notes: Company website fiix.io could not be fetched (DNS failure), treated as dead. Rockwell Automation's Fiix (CMMS) is a different company and was excluded. Acquisition date: BetaKit says 30 Sept 2019, other coverage says 8 Oct 2019. Seed was reported as 2.2M CAD or about 1.8M USD; BetaKit says 1.9M. Pre seed prizes of 25K and 20K are not recorded as rounds. Founder education not found.
